stories.title: Elevators
stories.author: Jrh0203
summaryZh: 文章解析电梯调度算法的演进，从基础的 SCAN/LOOK 到更智能的 RSR（相对系统响应）算法。
对比 LOOK 与 RSR 在不同流量和建筑规模下的等待时间表现，揭示简单算法在特定场景下反而更优。
分析目的地派梯（Destination Dispatch）系统因缺乏灵活性，在多数情况下等待时间反而劣于传统上下按钮。
highlightsZh: RSR 算法每 5 秒重新优化调度，动态调整电梯分配以应对实时变化。
使用 p50/p90 等统计指标衡量等待时间分布，更贴近用户真实体验。
早高峰等潮汐 traffic 模式对电梯调度性能影响显著。
目的地派梯系统虽信息更全，但刚性分配导致适应性不足，反不如传统按钮。
提供可交互的电梯仿真模拟器，支持调节楼层、电梯数量、流量等参数。

comments.author: theodorejb
comments.textZhHtml: 我遇到过的最糟糕的情况是大型会议结束后，每个人都立即离开酒店。电梯在下行过程中很快就满了，但随后浪费时间在每个后续楼层停下来呼叫，即使没有其他人可以进入。电梯在每一层停下来，门打开，等待的人们看到已经挤满了人，门就关上，这样的情况在接下来的 15 层重复，最后到达底层，所有人都下车。如果算法能够知道电梯已完全满员，并且只停在目的地楼层，而不是沿途每个楼层都进行呼叫，那么效率会高得多。

comments.author: rz2k
comments.textZhHtml:
还有一个插队策略。假设刚刚在一座约 20 层的小型建筑的顶层屋顶平台上进行了一场演讲。不想排队一百人的人，可以走楼梯下一层，在电梯满员之前上呼叫电梯进入轿厢，乘上一层*，然后一直乘到底层。

为了防止骚乱，大楼可能应该部署一名持有消防钥匙的员工来手动操作电梯。

* 电梯在接到下行呼叫时会应答上行按钮呼叫。顶楼，但他们会在填写任何新的向下指示之前接听电话，因此您必须先骑到顶层。

comments.textZhHtml:
回到高中时，模拟不同的电梯算法是我在计算机科学课上实施的项目之一。这不是为了课程——AP CS 不需要任何实际编程之类的东西——但这是一个有趣的项目。

一个很酷的联系是，旋转磁盘硬盘 (HDD) 实际上有点像一个很长的电梯，只是缠绕在主轴上，而不是完全垂直。 SCAN算法实际上是一种磁盘调度算法！

stories.title: Read this before you buy that TV streaming stick
stories.titleZh: 购买电视流媒体棒前，请先看这篇
stories.author: speckx
summaryZh: Security experts have been sounding the alarm for years about the risks of using generic TV boxes that promise unlimited content streaming for a one-time fee, warning that they secretly rent the user’s Internet connection out to strangers. But a groundbreaking new analysis finds these devices also routinely spoof themselves as mobile phones clicking ads on AI-generated websites as part of a sprawling operation that seeks to defraud online merchants and advertising networks. Pedro Falé is a threat researcher with the security firm Bitsight. Falé told KrebsOnSecurity he was able to peer inside a vast and complex ad fraud network by registering an expired domain name that was used to coordinate fake ad clicks across a particularly popular brand of these streaming devices known as H96. An H96 TV streaming device currently advertised for sale on Amazon. Falé said the domain he scooped up was previously used for telemetry, periodically collecting full hardware information and the entire list of installed apps from tens of thousands of H96 streaming sticks plugged into television sets around the globe. But upon inspecting the traffic being funneled to the domain, he discovered nearly all of the TV boxes transmitting data claimed to be mobile phone models from a variety of manufacturers, including Samsung, Vivo, Huawei, and Xiaomi. “We noticed something was wildly wrong,” Falé said. “Multiple devices reporting to this factory Android TV Box backdoor were ‘phones.'” Image: Bitsight. The researcher found all of the devices reported having the same two apps installed, and that those apps were made by a company called Zhejiang Fengwo IoT Technology Ltd, an entity founded in 2019 in mainland China which operates an ad-publishing portfolio under the name Fengwo Group. Further investigation into the Fengwo Group revealed it has registered multiple patents that match the inner workings of these apps. “Bitsight TRACE identified several Hong Kong, Singapore, and single person ‘legal’ shell identities used to collect the monetization and traced the operation back to a mainland China company known as Zhejiang Fengwo IoT Technology Co., Ltd, which operates under the Fengwo Group,” Falé wrote in a report released today about their findings. Falé said an analysis of the apps shows they help to coordinate an ad fraud network that uses these H96 devices as a captive traffic source to click on ads at AI-generated websites operated by the Fengwo Group. Bitsight discovered the websites contain machine-generated news articles and graphics across a range of categories, including finance, health, education, gaming, music and food blogs. But they also found none of those sites displayed ads unless the device visiting the page matched the spoofed mobile profile of these H96 devices. AI DIGITAL HUMANS The domain for the Fengwo Group — fwgcloud[.]com — claims the company is “redefining the boundaries of human-AI interaction,” and that it has created more than 120,000 “AI digital humans” available to rent for everything from emotional companionship to 24/7 customer service and creative design. The homepage for fwgcloud dot com. Falé said the Fengwo Group’s domain shared its SSL certificate data with other domains associated with the apps found on H96 devices, specifically the phone spoofing mechanism. He noted the domain also has an internal wiki platform that directly ties the Fengwo Group to a proprietary implementation of a Google-built visual programming language called Blockly, which was originally designed to help kids learn how to write software. According to Bitsight, the Fengwo Group’s employees use Blockly to build the sham websites, allowing low-skilled operators to drag blocks of code together in their Blockly editor — without any need to understand what the underlying code blocks do or how they work. The Blockly homepage. “An operator can drag blocks together in their Blockly editor, to define each fraud routine, given a task type,” reads Bitsight’s report. “Once the routine is saved, it gets exported as JavaScript and uploaded to the S3 buckets. An operator doesn’t need as much understanding of the underlying technicalities, as it is all set in place for ease of use.” Bitsight even found one of the Fengwo Group app developers mentioning exactly these advantages, noting the developer remarked that “only a small number of highly-skilled developers are needed to build the template execution-unit images,” and that “developers who create execution units from those templates have significantly lower technical requirements, greatly reducing the company’s operating costs.” Falé said if a user’s H96 streaming stick is selected for a specific fraud task, it will be pushed the appropriate Blockly module according to the task desired, which can include silently launching a web browser, visiting websites, browsing pages, managing tabs, and clicking on ads. To ensure the TV boxes masquerading as mobile phones can reliably click on ads displayed via the AI-generated websites, the Fengwo group “fuses three vision and reasoning systems into a single interface,” allowing the bots to correctly identify an ad on the webpage and navigate the site much like a human would, the Bitsight report observed. Examples of ad landing pages linked to the Fengwo Group. Image: Bitsight. TV ON? PROXY. TV OFF? AD FRAUD Bitsight found the H96 devices were either relaying residential proxy traffic or participating in ad fraud, but never both at the same time. In fact, they concluded that when these TV boxes detect an HDMI signal from an attached television — indicating the user intends to stream video content — the box is usually functioning as a residential proxy. When the TV is off, it switches back to waiting for ad fraud jobs. Falé said he believes the TV boxes are set up this way because its ad fraud activities are far more resource intensive and could interfere with the device’s stated purpose — streaming video content over the Internet. Despite repeated warnings from the FBI and security industry leaders about the security and privacy risks of using these streaming devices, major e-commerce providers like Amazon, Best Buy, Newegg and others continue to sell hundreds of different models and brands that bundle unofficial versions of Google’s Android operating system and are frequently marketed (via online influencers) as a way to access a broad array of streaming services and live broadcasts without a subscription. Image: fbi.gov. In addition to enlisting the user’s TV box in ad fraud networks, these off-brand streaming devices almost universally come with residential proxy software pre-installed. This software rents the user’s Internet address out to anonymous paying customers, who run the gamut from aggressive content scraping firms to ticket scalpers and outright cybercriminals. What’s more, because these generic (and generally dirt cheap) TV boxes are all horribly insecure by default and bereft of any kind of authentication, installing one on your home or office network only invites further mischief. In January, the proxy tracking service Synthient documented how multiple botnets had rapidly enslaved millions of TV boxes using a complex interplay of security vulnerabilities in both the residential proxy software and the streaming devices themselves. SHOW ME THE MONEY Bitsight said it tracked approximately 38,000 TV boxes globally phoning home to the expired Fengwo Group domain, and based on that number the report estimates this ad fraud network brings in revenues of close to $50,000 a day (not counting substantial revenue from the residential proxy side of the business). However, Falé emphasized that these estimates are highly conservative and based on telemetry from just one of the Fengwo Group’s core (but older) domains. As for the Fengwo Group’s claim to have 120,000 “digital humans” at their disposal, Bitsight’s report concludes it could be just a clever marketing scheme and/or a way to avoid drawing suspicion to the company’s operations. “Historically, when dealing with proxy services or DDoS, we sometimes see these websites undertake inconspicuous facades, so as not to advertise their DDoS capability or botnet size,” Falé wrote in the report. “This could also be the case here.” If the Fengwo Group truly does have tens of thousands of “AI humans” at its beck and call, it does not appear to have dedicated any of them to fielding inquiries from its own website. KrebsOnSecurity sought comment from the Fengwo Group by emailing the contact address listed on the company’s homepage, but the request bounced back with the reply, “Your message couldn’t be delivered to postmaster@fwgcloud[.]com. Their inbox is full, or it’s getting too much mail right now.” As Bitsight’s analysis shows, when it comes to TV boxes and streaming sticks, it’s best to stick to name brands from reputable manufacturers, and then to be sparing and careful with any apps you choose to install on the device — as many of those can bundle residential proxy software as well. Google says consumers can confirm whether or not a device is built with the official Android TV OS and Play Protect certification by following these instructions. Additionally, Synthient maintains a running list of IoT devices that have been known to ship to consumers with residential proxy software and other malicious apps pre-installed. Careful readers will notice Synthient’s list includes other IoT devices apart from streaming sticks and boxes: As the FBI has warned, residential proxy software has also been found in other popular consumer IoT devices from random brands, particularly digital photo frames.

stories.title: Google fixed more Chrome bugs in June than over the past two years, thanks to AI
stories.titleZh: 得益于人工智能，谷歌6月修复的Chrome漏洞数量超过了过去两年的总和。
stories.author: Garbage
summaryZh: How Chrome is using AI to improve vulnerability discovery, triage, and patching.

comments.author: userbinator
comments.textZhHtml:
还有待观察的是，由于 AI，Google 在 6 月份是否引入了比过去两年更多的 Chrome 错误。

最大的问题是，AI 输出可能非常令人信服，看起来“正确”，甚至看起来有效，直到您详细检查它并意识到它无法处理的所有边缘情况。

comments.author: karmasimida
comments.textZhHtml: 让我们对自己说实话，目前人工智能审查比人类更好，尤其是顶级模型。并不是说对于像 Chrome 这样的重要项目，您可以跳过审查更改。远非如此。但它可能已经比大多数人类开发者更好、更彻底了。

comments.author: StevePrefontain
comments.textZhHtml: 它并不比人工审查更出色。它擅长捕捉那些显而易见的基础问题，但往往会要求编写过度防御性的代码，去处理那些根本不存在的边缘情况，或是技术栈中其他环节早已处理过的问题。它会产生大量噪音，给出的评论往往缺乏实质价值。它基本上完全无法识别那些风险最高的问题，比如系统集成、业务层面的正确性等等。

comments.author: prymitive
comments.textZhHtml: 客观地说，还有一点值得注意：在现有代码中找出一个存在缺陷的边界情况，要比编写出毫无边界情况且完全无错的代码容易得多。阅读具体的逻辑并找出其中的漏洞，远比从零开始并最终实现完美要容易得多。这一点无论对人类还是智能体都适用，不过智能体在验证正确性方面表现得更为出色。

comments.author: karmasimida
comments.textZhHtml: 是的，这正是模型在这方面更具优势的原因：它们能够同等地（从机会均等的角度）关注其上下文窗口中的所有内容。

comments.author: unknownfuture
comments.textZhHtml:
呃，它在某些方面还挺在行，但其他方面就一般般了。

我现在的代码审查方式已经发生了转变。我不再细究具体的语义细节。在评估一段代码是否实现了作者的预期功能方面，AI的表现不亚于我，甚至比我更出色。

相反，我的工作是识别设计与架构异味、更宏观的语义错误、违背隐性业务需求等等。

例如，我最近在审查一段构建事务流程的代码。该流程的一部分涉及在用户可见的位置记录事务，并 我 我知道那应该在交易确认后才发生，但AI却将其实现为在交易发布时执行。

这起初是需求定义不充分的问题，但这 总是 现实世界中发生的一切。因此，这正是我能提供最有价值见解的地方：结合这一背景进行评估，无论是业务、运营、历史还是前瞻性方面。

stories.author: ai2027
summaryZh: Google DeepMind 发布 Gemini Robotics 2，为机器人提供全身智能控制、灵巧操作和多机器人协作能力。
包含三个核心模型：VLA 模型控制全身动作、ER 模型负责高层推理与任务规划、On-Device 模型支持端侧快速适配新机器人本体。
Gemini Robotics ER 2 已在 Google AI Studio 和 Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform 提供预览，VLA 和端侧模型面向早期合作伙伴开放。
highlightsZh: 首次实现人形机器人全身控制，可完成行走、蹲下、伸展及物体操作等复杂动作。

引入多机器人协作，不同类型机器人可协同完成复杂工作流。
端侧模型可在数小时内适配全新机器人本体，无需网络连接即可运行。

最初的证明难道不是类似于“当预言机说它会停机时，程序就无限循环；当预言机说它不会停机时，程序就立即停止”吗？其核心要点在于，你可以构造一个自相矛盾的程序，就其本质而言，任何预言机都无法判定它。

```python
source_code = open(__file__, 'rt').read()

response = ask_llm("will this program halt, only answer 'yes' or 'no'?\n" + source_code)

will_halt = response == 'yes'

while will_halt:

   continue
```

stories.title: Stacked PRs are now live on GitHub
stories.titleZh: 堆叠式 PR 现已在 GitHub 上线。
stories.author: tomzorz
summaryZh: GitHub 正式推出 Stacked PRs（堆叠式拉取请求）功能，进入公开预览阶段。
该功能允许将大型变更拆分为多个有序、可独立审查的小型 PR，并支持一键合并整个堆叠。
Next.js 团队已使用该功能数月，显著提升了代码审查效率和大型功能的交付速度。
highlightsZh: Stacked PRs 解决了大型 PR 难以审查和手动 rebase 多分支的痛点。
支持并行审查多个小型 PR，同时保持代码质量和分支保护策略。
可选择合并整个堆叠或逐层合并，灵活性高。
与 GitHub 现有的审查、检查和合并要求无缝集成，开箱即用。
Vercel Next.js 团队背书，验证了实际开发场景中的有效性。

comments.author: matharmin
comments.textZhHtml:
我已经使用了预览版一段时间，我很惊讶地看到他们扩展了预览版并有这么多未解决的问题。

例如，合并整个堆栈在许多情况下完全被破坏：https://github.com/github/gh-stack/discussions/212

您可以逐一合并，但如果您使用挤压和合并，则需要一个如果您需要审核，请重新批准堆栈中的每个 PR。这使您失去了可以说是堆叠 PR 的最大收益。

命令行工具（gh stack）有助于减少手动操作，但您仍然需要非常了解 git rebase 的工作原理，该工具只是帮助跨多个分支实现自动化。例如，如果您的本地分支与远程分支不同步，则仅运行 UI 建议的“gh stack rebase”命令将不起作用，并且工具不会向您指出这一点。

我确实发现堆栈 UI 非常好。与独立 PR 相比，它相当小，但足以显示它们之间的关系。

（我的评论都假设您已经有充分的理由堆叠 PR。此工具只是帮助简化工作流程，它没有提供任何新功能）

comments.author: sameenkarim
comments.textZhHtml:
我们正在针对挤压合并问题推出一系列错误修复。

我们有一个称为 CPRMC（创建拉取请求合并提交）的内部系统，用于评估 PR 是否“准备好”合并。这涵盖了从可合并性（检查合并冲突）到规则评估（确保批准与合并将创建的潜在提交相匹配）等所有内容。

当压缩合并多个 PR 堆栈时，这变得特别困难，因为我们必须计算一系列压缩的提交，然后将它们关联回规则/评论。这对于第一个 PR 来说相对容易，但对于第二个 PR 以后，这会变得更加复杂，因为祖先提交被压缩并且不按原样存在于分支上。我不会讨论多父母情况会变得多么复杂，哈哈。

这是我们需要解决的问题，也是团队的首要任务。我们的数据显示，99% 的堆栈合并成功完成，但我们需要提高得更高。

感谢您成为预览版的早期用户并在我们解决这些问题时与我们合作！

comments.author: Game_Ender
comments.textZhHtml:
您能确保对堆栈有良好的 API 支持吗？

我们使用自定义合并队列，我们希望它能够从堆栈中获取多个 PR一次作为单独的 PR。 最后我检查过你必须登陆一个 PR、重新设置堆栈基础、登陆下一个等等。 与简单地并行测试部分或全部堆栈然后声明它们合并相比，这在 CI 时间（和挂钟时间）方面非常昂贵。 本质上，在队列完成其任务后，机器人需要能够说“挤压合并这 3 个堆叠的 PR”。

comments.author: sameenkarim
comments.textZhHtml:
是的，这是我们的首要任务之一。其一，所有堆栈操作都有一个完全公开的 API 。因此，如果您不想使用 `gh stack` CLI，您可以构建自己的：https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/stacks

对于合并，我们有一个 API，但必须将其移至新的异步方法：https://github.github.io/gh-stack/reference/merge-api/

旧版 API 是完全同步的，并且由于多个 PR 的堆栈通常需要 10 秒以上（我们的全局超时），因此我们必须转向异步。

我们已经有一些人使用它来将堆栈集成到他们的合并队列中。 最重要的是，您可以在一个原子操作中获得多个 PR，然后将多个 PR 的所有提交一次推送到 main。因此，不必为每个重新运行构建/部署，它可以触发包含所有更改的最后一次提交。

另外，外部合并又如何？在本地合并或通过外部工具合并时，有没有办法与堆栈进行理智的交互？

comments.textZhHtml:
您好 - 过去一个月，我们与 Sameen 和 GitHub 团队合作，在合并队列中获得了对堆栈的支持：https://trunk.io/blog/trunk-merge-queue-now-supports-github-...

他们确实拥有可在合并队列中使用的 API，我很高兴分享我们如何构建它的说明，以便您可以将其添加到合并队列中。

comments.textZhHtml: Trunk 是使用 GitHub 的 API 来合并堆栈，还是在内部/自行完成集成？

comments.author: mattmatheson

stories.title: The session you cannot take with you
stories.author: apitman
summaryZh: The original promise of an inference API was wonderfully simple: send some input, receive some output. If you kept both, you had the conversation. You could inspect it, archive it, replay it, or give it to a different model. That abstraction was never completely true. For instance prompt caches live on somebody else's GPUs, tokenization differs between models, and sampling is not reproducible (and quite intentionally so). But the semantic record of a session in the form of a transcript could still belong to the user. A transcript should contain the instructions, messages, tool calls and tool results. Another sufficiently capable model might not continue identically, but it could understand what happened and take over. Inference APIs are frustratingly moving away from that property, at least somewhat. They increasingly return a mixture of text and provider-bound state that is very intentionally non-portable.

reasoning tokens that are billed to the user but returned only as opaque, encrypted blobs, with useless summaries at best web searches where the model sees source material the client never sees compacted context that only the original provider can decrypt subagent instructions and messages hidden from the application running the agents in the form of encrypted payloads file, vector-store, container, and cache references that cannot be resolved anywhere else. response and conversation state that is entirely keyed by IDs that are stored fully on the provider's servers

stories.author: dmantis

此举旨在为Android用户提供更安全的体验，特别是针对未成年用户的保护。
highlightsZh: Google Play将引入年龄信号API以支持更安全的用户体验。

comments.textZhHtml: 没错。这就是我对“仅限成人”标签感到不满的地方。理想情况下，这个标签也不应该有“适合儿童”的选项，因为一个家长认为安全的内容，在另一个家长看来可能完全合适。我认为互联网内容评级协会的思路是对的，即标签只需显示网站是否包含特定类型的内容，而由家长自己决定审查的程度。
